about: Core tier of the Formula reaction codex (Phase 1). Every entry is balanced and has a source; check is 'reviewed' after the internal science review of 2026-11-04 (a teacher review comes later, for school systems). See docs/chem/README.md.

reactions.name: Methane burns

reactions.name: Lithium hydroxide meets acid
reactions.say: A base and an acid make lithium chloride and water.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Sulfuric acid meets base
reactions.say: Each sulfuric acid needs two sodium hydroxides, one for each of its two hydrogens.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Potassium sulfate forms
reactions.say: Potassium hydroxide neutralises sulfuric acid.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Nitric acid meets base
reactions.say: Nitric acid and sodium hydroxide make sodium nitrate and water.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Making saltpetre
reactions.say: Potassium hydroxide and nitric acid make potassium nitrate.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Ammonia meets hydrogen chloride
reactions.say: Two gases meet and make a white smoke of ammonium chloride.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Slaked lime meets acid
reactions.say: Lime neutralises acid, which is how farmers fix sour soil.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Vinegar meets base
reactions.say: Vinegar's acetic acid is neutralised into sodium acetate and water.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Making fertiliser salt
reactions.say: Ammonia and sulfuric acid make ammonium sulfate fertiliser.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Making ammonium nitrate
reactions.say: Ammonia and nitric acid make ammonium nitrate fertiliser.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Barium hydroxide meets sulfuric acid
reactions.say: Neutralisation and a white precipitate of barium sulfate at the same time.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Carbon dioxide is soaked up
reactions.say: Sodium hydroxide soaks up carbon dioxide, making sodium carbonate.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Black powder turns blue
reactions.say: Copper oxide dissolves in warm sulfuric acid into blue copper sulfate.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Magnesium oxide meets acid
reactions.say: A metal oxide is a base, so it neutralises acid.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Zinc dissolves in acid
reactions.say: Zinc fizzes in acid and gives off hydrogen.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Magnesium dissolves in acid
reactions.say: Magnesium fizzes fast in acid and gives off hydrogen.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Iron dissolves in acid
reactions.say: Iron slowly fizzes in hydrochloric acid, making pale green iron(II) chloride.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Aluminium dissolves in acid
reactions.say: Once its oxide skin is gone, aluminium fizzes in acid.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Calcium dissolves in acid
reactions.say: Calcium fizzes hard in acid and gives off hydrogen.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Zinc meets sulfuric acid
reactions.say: The lab way to make hydrogen gas.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Magnesium meets sulfuric acid
reactions.say: Magnesium fizzes in sulfuric acid and makes magnesium sulfate.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Iron meets sulfuric acid
reactions.say: Iron dissolves in dilute sulfuric acid, giving hydrogen.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Copper meets nitric acid
reactions.say: Copper won't dissolve in most acids, but nitric acid oxidises it and gives nitric oxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Chalk meets acid
reactions.say: Acid fizzes on chalk or marble and releases carbon dioxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Washing soda meets acid
reactions.say: A carbonate and an acid give salt, water and carbon dioxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Baking soda meets acid
reactions.say: Baking soda neutralises acid and releases carbon dioxide; the mix cools.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Green powder turns blue
reactions.say: Copper carbonate fizzes in acid and makes blue copper sulfate.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Acid rain on marble
reactions.say: Sulfuric acid eats marble statues and leaves calcium sulfate.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Magnesium carbonate meets acid
reactions.say: Gym chalk fizzes in acid and releases carbon dioxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Iron nail turns copper
reactions.say: Iron pushes copper out of solution; the nail turns copper-coloured.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Zinc meets copper sulfate
reactions.say: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it takes copper's place.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Magnesium meets copper sulfate
reactions.say: Magnesium pushes copper out fast and gets hot.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Aluminium meets copper sulfate
reactions.say: Once its oxide skin is broken, aluminium pushes copper out.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Magnesium meets zinc sulfate
reactions.say: Magnesium is above zinc in reactivity, so it takes zinc's place.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Lead tree
reactions.say: Zinc pushes lead out of solution as grey crystals.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Silver tree
reactions.say: Copper wire grows silver crystals and the liquid turns blue.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Zinc meets silver nitrate
reactions.say: Zinc pushes silver out of solution.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Thermite
reactions.say: Aluminium steals oxygen from rust so violently it makes molten iron, far too hot to put out with water.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Blast furnace
reactions.say: Carbon monoxide takes the oxygen out of iron ore, leaving iron.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Copper from its ore
reactions.say: Hot carbon takes oxygen from copper oxide, leaving copper metal.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Hydrogen reduces copper oxide
reactions.say: Hot hydrogen turns black copper oxide back into shiny copper.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Zinc from its ore
reactions.say: Very hot carbon frees zinc from zinc oxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Magnesium burns in CO2
reactions.say: Burning magnesium is so hungry for oxygen it takes it from carbon dioxide, leaving soot.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Peroxide frees iodine
reactions.say: Hydrogen peroxide turns iodide into brown iodine in acid.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Chlorine frees bromine
reactions.say: Chlorine is more reactive, so it pushes bromine out; the liquid turns orange.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Chlorine frees iodine
reactions.say: Chlorine pushes iodine out of potassium iodide; the liquid turns brown.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Bromine frees iodine
reactions.say: Bromine pushes iodine out, because bromine is more reactive.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Making bleach
reactions.say: Chlorine bubbled into cold sodium hydroxide makes household bleach.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Iron burns in chlorine
reactions.say: Hot iron wool glows in chlorine and makes brown iron(III) chloride.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Aluminium meets iodine
reactions.say: A drop of water starts a fierce reaction with purple iodine fumes.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Zinc meets iodine
reactions.say: Zinc and iodine join into zinc iodide when water helps them mix.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Magnesium meets nitrogen
reactions.say: Burning magnesium even joins with nitrogen, making magnesium nitride.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Lithium meets nitrogen
reactions.say: Lithium is one of the few metals that joins with nitrogen at room temperature.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Copper meets sulfur
reactions.say: Hot copper and sulfur join into black copper(I) sulfide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Zinc meets sulfur
reactions.say: Zinc and sulfur powder react in a flash to make zinc sulfide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Hydrogen meets sulfur
reactions.say: Hydrogen over hot sulfur makes smelly hydrogen sulfide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Sodium meets hydrogen
reactions.say: Hot sodium takes up hydrogen to make sodium hydride.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Silver tarnishes
reactions.say: Traces of hydrogen sulfide in air turn silver black.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Salt makes a cloud
reactions.say: Silver nitrate and salt make a white cloud of silver chloride. It is the test for chloride.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Cream precipitate
reactions.say: Silver nitrate and potassium bromide give pale cream silver bromide, used in old photographs.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Yellow precipitate
reactions.say: Silver nitrate and potassium iodide give yellow silver iodide, used to seed clouds.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Golden rain
reactions.say: Two clear liquids make bright yellow lead iodide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Test for sulfate
reactions.say: Barium chloride makes white barium sulfate with any sulfate.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Blue jelly
reactions.say: Sodium hydroxide makes a pale blue jelly of copper hydroxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Green precipitate
reactions.say: Iron(II) ions give a dirty green precipitate with sodium hydroxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Rust-brown precipitate
reactions.say: Iron(III) ions give a rust-brown precipitate with sodium hydroxide.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Making chalk
reactions.say: Two solutions make solid chalk that settles out; the mix cools very slightly.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: White precipitate
reactions.say: Magnesium ions give white magnesium hydroxide with a base.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Lead chloride settles
reactions.say: Lead nitrate and salt make white lead chloride.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Zinc hydroxide forms
reactions.say: Zinc ions give a white precipitate that dissolves again in more base.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Fizzy water
reactions.say: A little carbon dioxide dissolves and makes weak carbonic acid.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Acid rain starts
reactions.say: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in rain to make sulfurous acid.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Ammonia in water
reactions.say: Ammonia dissolves in water and makes it basic (written as ammonium hydroxide).
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Sodium oxide meets water
reactions.say: A metal oxide dissolves in water and makes a base.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Phosphoric acid forms
reactions.say: Phosphorus oxide grabs water fiercely and makes phosphoric acid.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Hydrogenation
reactions.say: A nickel catalyst adds hydrogen across a double bond, as in making margarine.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Bromine water test
reactions.say: Ethene takes up orange bromine, turning it colourless. It is the test for a double bond.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Ethanol from ethene
reactions.say: Steam adds to ethene over an acid catalyst, making ethanol.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Making a fruity ester
reactions.say: An acid and an alcohol join into ethyl ethanoate, which smells like pear drops.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e).

reactions.name: Methane meets chlorine
reactions.say: Light breaks chlorine apart and a chlorine atom takes a hydrogen's place.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Ethanol loses water
reactions.say: Hot ethanol over an acid catalyst loses water and becomes ethene.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Cracking oil
reactions.say: Big oil molecules are cracked into petrol and ethene.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Sugar splits in two
reactions.say: An enzyme splits table sugar into glucose and fructose (both C6H12O6).
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Ozone forms
reactions.say: Electric sparks or UV light turn oxygen into ozone, which smells sharp.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Ozone splits
reactions.say: Ozone breaks back into oxygen; high in the sky this soaks up UV light.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Brown gas pales
reactions.say: Brown nitrogen dioxide pairs up into colourless dinitrogen tetroxide when cooled.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Making glass
reactions.say: Sand and soda ash melt together, releasing carbon dioxide (soda glass, simplified).
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Lime meets sand
reactions.say: At furnace heat, limestone and sand make calcium silicate (simplified; cement clinker is richer in calcium).
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).

reactions.name: Touch powder
reactions.say: Nitrogen triiodide explodes at a touch into nitrogen and purple iodine. Only trained chemists handle tiny amounts.
reactions.source: Standard school chemistry reaction; see OpenStax Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e). Heat direction from standard enthalpies of formation (NIST Chemistry WebBook).
